overview: The MPS Curriculum, Instruction, Assessment & Accountability subcommittee oversees the district's educational frameworks, subject-area curricula, instructional resources, and student assessment systems. The body has been meeting across recorded sessions from March 2021 through October 2026. Early meetings centered on detailed departmental reviews of English Language Arts, science, fine arts, health, and physical education curricula. In later meetings, the subcommittee shifted toward evaluating district-wide assessment practices, monitoring curriculum implementation fidelity, and planning for state-level policy changes. At its most recent meeting in October 2026, the subcommittee reviewed the district's comprehensive assessment landscape and evaluated Medford's readiness to adopt proposed state graduation frameworks following the elimination of the MCAS graduation requirement.

threads.name: English Language Arts curriculum
threads.summary: Humanities Director Dr. Nicole Chiesa presented an overview of the district's English Language Arts curriculum. The presentation detailed instructional resources, equity initiatives, program budget costs, and a multi-year timeline to pilot and select a new core reading program. District leadership also outlined plans to pilot a new elementary reading program.

threads.name: Science curriculum
threads.summary: Science Director Rocco Cieri presented an overview of K–12 science instruction across the district. The review highlighted state framework alignment, high school course sequences, and textbook needs for biology and chemistry. Department leaders also outlined instructional adjustments made during the pandemic.

threads.name: Fine arts curriculum
threads.summary: Dr. Bernadette Ricciardelli presented a review of the fine arts curriculum across all grade levels. The presentation addressed state framework revisions, online instructional tools such as Quaver Music, and student instrument access. Department leadership also outlined upcoming budgetary needs and pandemic-related instructional adjustments.

threads.name: Health and physical education curricula
threads.summary: Director of Physical Education and Health Education Rachel Perry presented the K–12 health curriculum based on the Michigan Model, which led to subcommittee discussion on puberty education, gender identity, and consent. Perry also outlined physical education programming, including motor skill progression in elementary and middle schools alongside high school electives like lifeguard training and CPR certification. Proposed departmental goals included adding middle school health and adaptive PE staff, updating professional development, and evaluating the FLASH curriculum for special education students.

threads.name: District assessment and curriculum monitoring
threads.summary: Assistant Superintendent Suzanne Galusi and department leaders presented an update on curriculum implementations across disciplines and discussed establishing an ongoing curriculum review process. Administration reviewed the use of NWEA MAP assessments, internal benchmarks, and cross-departmental standards to monitor curriculum fidelity and effectiveness. Later, Assistant Superintendent Kim Talbot presented a broader assessment landscape report covering classroom, district, state, and opt-in testing while emphasizing benchmarking data to inform instruction without excessive test preparation.

threads.name: State graduation frameworks
threads.summary: The subcommittee received an update on proposed state graduation frameworks following the elimination of the MCAS graduation requirement. Dr. Kim Talbot reviewed the state's proposed framework and evaluated the district's readiness to meet emerging requirements. The evaluation covered foundational coursework, end-of-course assessments, post-secondary planning, and culminating experiences.

periods.narrative: During this term, the subcommittee conducted comprehensive departmental reviews of the district's K–12 ELA, science, fine arts, health, and physical education curricula. Presentations outlined framework alignments, resource needs, pilot programs, and departmental priorities.

The subcommittee met with administration and curriculum leaders to examine curriculum status under the strategic plan and establish ongoing review processes. Discussions focused on using NWEA MAP assessments and internal benchmarks to monitor curriculum fidelity.
